en: Now, as you're building websites and web
applications with HTMX,
you sometimes might want to
run your own JavaScript code whenever some
event occurs.
For example, here in this application where
we have this form, we might want to
clear this form and clear this input in this
form whenever it's being submitted.
So we wanna listen to the submit event
that's triggered by this form, and then we
wanna run some custom JavaScript code to
clear this input.
And that's something where HTMX supports you
because HTMX has this hx-on
attribute, which you can add on elements to
listen to events that occur on those
elements or
on child elements if those events bubble up.
So you can use hx-on to listen to events
and you use hx-on such that you add it to
the element on which you wanna listen to
events.
And then you define the event to which you
wanna listen by adding a colon after hx-one
and then the event name.
For example, click if you wanna listen to
clicks on that form.
Of course, when listening to events, you
then typically also wanna control
what happens when that event occurs.
And you do that with help of the value you
assign to hx-on.
Because that value is then actually the
JavaScript code that should execute when an
event occurs.
Now here you could call
some function that might be defined in some
other file you're importing into this file,
but it can also be some inline code.
For example, here, if I wanna clear the
form, if I wanna clear this input, I can
achieve this by selecting this form and
calling the reset method on it. Because it
turns out that form elements and the
underlying objects to which you can get
access in JavaScript have a reset method,
this method here, which you can call to
reset all the inputs of that form.
Therefore, here for this event listener, we
just have to get access to the form and then
we can call reset on it.
Now we could get access by using
document.getElementById,
querySelector
and then select the form like this.
And this is now just some standard
JavaScript code which I'm writing inline
here as a value for this event listener,
which might look strange at first but which
is perfectly valid and indeed the
recommended way of using the hx-on
attribute.
And then on that form here, I could call
reset.
Now at the moment I'm listening to the click
event here and that might not be what I
want. So maybe here we wanna listen to the
submit event instead
so that whenever the form is submitted, we
clear it.
With this code added here and with this
change in place, if we reload
and I enter my text here, if I click add
goal, you see the form is cleared and the
rest still works as before. But now we also
listen to that event in addition.
